Wow, I didn't realize that this would be such an amazing game.

Hacknet, Uplink's spiritual successor. 

Developed by a one-man studio called Team Fractal Alligator, Hacknet is a terminal-based game that implements real UNIX codes and commands to bypass and/or shutdown firewalls, proxys, ports, etc., to gain access to other peoples' computers and eOS devices (game's parody of smartphones) for their information or information in general and retype false info for a cilent to help him, steal the infomation and expose it to light, or destroy the user's computer server.

The story for me so far is surpisingly good. To avoid spoilers, I'll keep it short. It involves a notorius hacker named Bit. He fails to reconnect to his system for 14 days, his failsafe kicks in, sending instructions in automated emails to you. It's up to you to find out why. 

You can get jobs from different entites, such as CSEC, to receive hack codes and malware injectors to help you along your cyber hacking adventure. Sadly, unlike Uplink, you don't earn money and you can't upgrade your computer, RAM, CPU, etc. 

Lots of little secrets here and there, some computers have little chat logs from other users for a fun read. The music is good, nice tempo beat to it. 

Overall, it's a fun terminal-based hackers game with a modern day retouch.

This is, hands down, the best hacker game I've played so far. 

There is no finance system, which is great. Means you can do the missions/assignements/whatever you call them just to help out and progress with the story. You don't have to grind dozens of copy-pasted "download file from a server" missions just to buy a software tool or a faster CPU. 

The missions are usually pretty straightforward, although some could use more of a clear objective along the lines of "reply to this email with the password to THAT server". Some missions, though... Project Juno... Best. Mission. Ever. You start with an IP address, you go and poke and come up with a link or another IP address hidden in some memo, or even a password to something you can't hack and you basically explore the net and look for a solution while nobody knows if a solution exists (well, it does, since this is a game, but you get the idea). The final mission and dtory outcome feel a bit underwhelming, but all-in-all, very nice game of holywood hacking.

The only thing that sucks is the music. Not a fan of techno, but most hacker games seem to have it. Is this a thing? Like another stereotype of hacker = shy, socially awekward nerd with zits and dorky glasses, who listens to techno? Anyway, that doesn't drag the overall experience down. If you liked Uplink, get this. If you like hacker movies/games, get this. If you type like a toddler, go practice, then get this.

Following in the footsteps of the great Introversion hit Uplink, Hacknet is another hacking game.  Where Uplink is more of an open world game with randomly generated missions, Hacknet is a campaign game, you play through a storyline, ultimately investigating the death of a hacker called Bit.  This means that you have richer content in all areas of the game rather than "similar" generated missions but fewer missions to play.  It's not a downside, just different.  In my opinion if you loved Uplink you'll love this.  It's a much more graphically rich game, just look at it!  But yet you'll spend much more time typing commands than in Uplink.

tl;dr
I can't recommend this enough, great storyline, great gameplay, want more.

After playing this game for a few hours, I felt compelled to write a review.  I play a lot of the mainstream types of games, but when I saw Hacknet on sale, I figured that it wouldn't hurt to broaden my spectrum.  What I got was a great text based game, where I actualy felt the exhilaration of hacking.  Am I really hacking like real hackers do in the real-world?  Probably not, but that's ok, because it feels like I am, and that's not a rabbit-hole I wish to delve into.

The beginning missions do just enough to teach you what you need to know without holding your hand too much to the point where you go looking for the toggle switch to "turn off hints".  Sure you hack into computers and you feel cool, but it's not until the first hack that you're being traced and there's a timer ticking, that the adrenaline really starts to kick in.

The puzzles are just difficult enough that you don't want to look to a guide, and feel rewarded when you succeed.

I can't tell you much about the story, as I feel like I'm still in the phase where the game is making sure I'm ready to venture into the story, but I'm having a blast just thinking about all the trouble I'm about to get into.  It's a game I have a hard time putting down, and an even harder time being away from.  Whether you catch this game on sale, or pay full price, you'll definitely feel like you've made a solid purchase.

Loved this game.  It has all the elements that I was looking for since playing Uplink.  
- Console based interface balances well with a graphical interface.
- Visually pleasing animations
- Fun "against the clock" visuals 
- It doesn't "punish" the user too much for failure. (Which is how I felt about Uplink)
- Great story element
- Excellen use of flavor text

The good far out weighs the bad, but I'll include a few things that I didn't like just to for honesty:
- The network map gets a little crowded.
- The note system seemed to take up more memory than it should 
- No upgrade system, therefore no sense of reward.  But this was more of a linear story, so that's to be expected.
- Too linear.  It's a story driven game.  Each mission is designed to take you on to the next.  Once you're done, you're done.
- The network map gets a bit crowded towards the end.

If you were to make a Hacknet 2, please pleasel PLEASE make it more sand-box like.  Auto generating missions, an embedded story element that doens't end the game, an upgrade/cash system, aybe a defense based system to deflect incoming attacks.  These are the things that I crave.
